description: We are a team of five students interested in science, technology and engineering.
summary:
Our project combines robotics, augmented reality (AR), and interactive web technology to bring the history of Mars exploration to life.

At its core is a custom built, remote controlled Mars rover powered by a Raspberry Pi 4B, which hosts the website and transmits live data over Wi-Fi to other devices. The rover is operated using a DualSense controller and equipped with a camera, a robotic arm, and various electronic components. Through the website, users can explore Mars and other planets, select historical rovers and satellites, and project them into the rover's live camera feed. AR technology further enhances the experience by overlaying a virtual Martian landscape onto the real world, while specially designed cubes represent virtual rocks that serve as essential mission objectives.

The project recreates the final moments of real Mars rover missions, challenging users to complete tasks such as collecting samples and navigating to designated coordinates. To ensure historical accuracy, we based our research on official NASA publications and mission reports.

Our main goal is to inspire younger generations to discover the wonders of space exploration. By combining hands on robotics with immersive storytelling, we aim to make space science more accessible, engaging, and educational. Above all, we want to show that even missions that have ended continue to shape our understanding of the universe and contribute to the technology we use today.
details:
1. What does the project do and how does it work?

LAST.SOL combines robotics, augmented reality (AR), and web technology to recreate historical Mars rover missions. Users control a custom-built rover using a DualSense controller, complete missions, collect virtual samples, and explore planets through an interactive website and AR.

2. What benefits does the project have?

It makes learning about space more engaging and interactive. Students develop problem-solving skills and gain knowledge about space exploration, robotics, programming, and modern technology.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Our goal is to inspire younger generations to explore space science and STEM. We want to show that learning about space can be both educational and fun, while preserving the legacy of historical missions.

4. How is the project creative?

We combine a physical rover with AR, virtual environments, and interactive missions. Instead of just reading about space exploration, users can experience historical missions themselves.

5. What factors did our team consider?

We focused on educational value, historical accuracy, ease of use, technical possibilities, and our target audience. We used official NASA materials for research.

6. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

1. Web Development & Programming

  • Svelte and SvelteKit
  • TypeScript
  • Python
  • Node.js and npm
  • Tailwind CSS
  • Vite
  • Chromium Browser

2. Robotics & Hardware

  • Raspberry Pi
  • Raspberry Pi Camera
  • IMU 6050
  • Motors and servos
  • H-bridge
  • DualSense Gamepad
  • Raspbian Linux

3. Computer Vision, AR & AI

  • Three.js
  • ONNX Runtime Web with WebGPU
  • OpenCV
  • OpenCV.js
  • MediaMTX
  • WebRTC

4. 3D Design & Manufacturing

  • Autodesk Fusion 360
  • OrcaSlicer
  • Klipper
  • Ender 5 Pro
  • TPU and PLA filaments

5. Testing & Development Tools

  • Storybook
  • Vitest
  • Git
  • Claude Code
  • OpenAI Codex
